method: Both articles fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Claims are verbatim-checked against the retrieved text of their own source with scripts/verify.py --only-source. This guideline deliberately holds BOTH the review and the published letters contesting it, because the dispute is unresolved in print and a prescriber should know it exists; contested claims are marked at the point of the claim rather than silently resolved in favour of either side. Declared conflicts of interest on both sides are recorded as claims. The nonhormonal dose table is a grid rendered as text; values are verbatim but column alignment is a transcription risk. Estrogen doses are NOT stated in the source (it refers to an Australasian Menopause Society guide) and none is reconstructed.

claims.claim: Average age of menopause in Australia is 51
claims.source_text: The average age of menopause in Australian women is 51 years

claims.claim: Definitions of menopause stages
claims.source_text: menopause- the final menstrual period or the permanent cessation of ovarian function … early menopause- menopause occurring at 40 to 44 years of age … perimenopause- from when the menstrual cycle starts … changing until 12 months after menopause … postmenopause- from 12 months after menopause

claims.claim: 75% experience symptoms, 25% moderate to severe
claims.source_text: Approximately 75% of women experience symptoms during perimenopause and after menopause, with 25% experiencing moderate to severe symptoms affecting their quality of life

claims.claim: Common symptom list including cognitive and musculoskeletal
claims.source_text: vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes, night sweats) … cognitive concerns ('brain fog') … sleep disturbance … musculoskeletal symptoms … formication (sensation of insects crawling under the skin) … genitourinary symptoms (vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency, urinary frequency, recurrent urinary tract infections)

claims.claim: The article restricts women to cisgender women
claims.source_text: In this article, the term 'women' only refers to cisgender women. Trans- and gender-diverse people may also experience menopausal symptoms and may benefit from appropriately tailored health services

claims.claim: MHT is recommended in premature ovarian insufficiency regardless of symptoms
claims.source_text: Menopausal hormone therapy is recommended for women with premature ovarian insufficiency (menopause occurring before 40 years of age) regardless of symptoms, unless contraindicated

claims.claim: MHT until usual age of menopause in POI to reduce osteoporosis and CVD risk
claims.source_text: MHT is recommended regardless of symptoms (unless contraindicated) until the usual age of menopause, to reduce the risks of osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease

claims.claim: MHT is the most effective treatment offered after individualised discussion
claims.source_text: Menopausal hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for menopausal symptoms. It can be offered to symptomatic patients with no contraindications following an individualised discussion about the risk of harms versus benefits

claims.claim: MHT regimens
claims.source_text: estrogen-only for women who have had a total hysterectomy; unopposed estrogen is associated with endometrial hyperplasia and potential malignancy … cyclic combined MHT-continuous estrogen with a progestogen given cyclically (e.g. for 12 to 14 continuous days of a calendar month) … continuous combined MHT-continuous estrogen and progestogen … tibolone for women more than one year after menopause, particularly those with low libido

claims.claim: Cyclic for perimenopausal, continuous combined for postmenopausal
claims.source_text: For perimenopausal women, cyclic MHT is used, where a progestogen is given cyclically with estrogen … For postmenopausal women, continuous combined MHT is used, where a progestogen is given continuously with estrogen

claims.claim: Continuous combined in perimenopause causes irregular bleeding
claims.source_text: If continuous combined MHT is used by perimenopausal women, irregular bleeding frequently occurs; cyclic MHT is recommended to minimise irregular bleeding. Once a woman has been using cyclic MHT for 12 months, a trial of continuous combined MHT can take place

claims.claim: Estradiol preferred and started low to medium
claims.source_text: Estradiol is preferred because it is structurally similar to 17-beta-estradiol, the commonest naturally occurring estrogen in premenopausal women … Systemic estrogen should be started at a low-to-medium dose and adjusted according to symptoms

claims.claim: Topical vaginal estrogen is only for genitourinary symptoms and needs no progestogen
claims.source_text: Topical vaginal estrogen is only appropriate for managing genitourinary symptoms. Low-dose vaginal estrogen (estradiol or estriol) … is available as vaginal tablets, pessaries or creams and does not require the addition of a progestogen

claims.claim: Progestogen options and absence of RCT data
claims.source_text: Several progestogens are available for use in MHT (e.g. micronised progesterone, dydrogesterone, drospirenone, norethisterone, medroxyprogesterone acetate) … No randomised controlled trial data are available to guide choice

claims.claim: Micronised progesterone and dydrogesterone considered first line
claims.source_text: Micronised progesterone and dydrogesterone (which is structurally similar to natural progesterone) may have a lower breast cancer risk than older synthetic progestogens … and, for most women, are considered first line

claims.claim: 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD for up to 5 years with estrogen
claims.source_text: the 52 mg levonorgestrel-releasing IUD, can be used for up to 5 years in combination with estrogen. It has the added benefit of providing contraception and managing heavy menstrual bleeding

claims.claim: Combined oral contraceptive as MHT under 50
claims.source_text: Women younger than 50 years of age, without contraindications, can use combined hormonal contraception such as a combined oral contraceptive pill for MHT

claims.claim: Tibolone dosing and fracture data
claims.source_text: The usual dose is 2.5 mg orally, daily … Clinical trials have demonstrated low-dose tibolone (e.g. 1.25 mg orally, daily) may reduce both vertebral and nonvertebral fractures

claims.claim: Tibolone cautions
claims.source_text: Tibolone should only be prescribed to women who are more than one year after menopause as it can cause vaginal bleeding. Women with a history of breast cancer should not be prescribed tibolone. Tibolone is associated with increased risk of stroke in women older than 60 years of age

claims.claim: MHT adverse effects and review schedule
claims.source_text: Women starting on MHT must be warned about adverse effects, including nausea and breast tenderness. Women should be reviewed after 6 to 12 weeks of starting MHT … Annual reassessment is recommended to ensure health screening is up to date and to review the need for ongoing treatment

claims.claim: Bleeding beyond 6 months should be investigated
claims.source_text: bleeding and spotting often settles over months, but if it persists beyond 6 months, or becomes heavy or prolonged, it should be investigated

claims.claim: No maximal duration of MHT is defined
claims.source_text: There is no maximal duration of MHT defined

claims.claim: Contraindications to MHT
claims.source_text: hormone-dependent cancers including breast and endometrial … undiagnosed vaginal bleeding … acute cardiovascular event … acute venous thromboembolism … porphyria cutanea tarda … severe liver disease

claims.claim: Conditions where caution is recommended
claims.source_text: past myocardial infarction, transient ischaemic attack or stroke … high risk of venous thromboembolism … active liver disease … migraine with aura … hypertriglyceridaemia … hepatobiliary disease … age older than 65 years and no prior use of MHT

claims.claim: Notes on the precautions box including treated hypertension
claims.source_text: MHT is generally safe to use in patients with treated stage 1 endometrial malignancy … Consider transdermal estrogen for MHT if the patient is anticoagulated … Exercise caution with oral estrogen; transdermal estrogen is preferred for MHT … Treated hypertension is not a contraindication to MHT use

claims.claim: When transdermal is preferred
claims.source_text: a history of atherosclerotic heart disease or stroke … a history of migraine with aura … treated cardiovascular disease risk factors (e.g. hypertension, dyslipidaemia) … increased risk of venous thromboembolism … hepatobiliary disease

claims.claim: Oral estrogen and VTE mechanism
claims.source_text: Oral estrogen undergoes first-pass metabolism in the liver and alters the hepatic production of coagulation factors. This is associated with a 2- to 3-fold increase in venous thromboembolism, but the absolute risk remains low … Transdermal estrogen does not carry this risk

claims.claim: Nonhormonal drugs are less effective and mostly limited by adverse effects
claims.source_text: Generally, nonhormonal drugs are less effective than MHT and do not confer the bone- or cardiovascular-protective benefits of estrogen. Most of the drugs have limited use because of their adverse effects

claims.claim: Nonhormonal drug doses
claims.source_text: serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors desvenlafaxine 25 to 150 mg orally daily dizziness, nausea, sexual dysfunction venlafaxine 37.5 to 150 mg orally daily selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors citalopram 10 to 20 mg orally daily dizziness, nausea, sexual dysfunction escitalopram 5 to 20 mg orally daily paroxetine [NB2] 10 to 25 mg orally daily

claims.claim: Clonidine gabapentin and oxybutynin doses
claims.source_text: clonidine [NB3] 25 to 75 micrograms orally twice daily dizziness, drowsiness, constipation gabapentin 100 to 900 mg orally daily in up to 3 divided doses drowsiness, dizziness, possible withdrawal symptoms oxybutynin [NB4] 2.5 to 5 mg orally twice daily dry mouth, drowsiness, blurred vision

claims.claim: All but clonidine are not TGA registered for vasomotor symptoms
claims.source_text: All drugs listed in the table, except clonidine, are not registered by the Therapeutic Goods Administration for treating vasomotor symptoms

claims.claim: Paroxetine and tamoxifen interaction
claims.source_text: Paroxetine should not be co-administered with tamoxifen; co-administration can cause inhibition of cytochrome P450 2D6 and reduce the efficacy of tamoxifen

claims.claim: Clonidine no longer recommended and oxybutynin cognitive risk
claims.source_text: Clonidine may be used but is no longer recommended because of its adverse effects … Oxybutynin may help symptoms of overactive bladder; however, it may cause adverse effects, particularly cognitive decline in older people

claims.claim: Genitourinary symptoms do not improve with time
claims.source_text: Unlike vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary symptoms do not improve with time. Nonhormonal lubricants can be helpful for vaginal dryness

claims.claim: Complementary and compounded bioidentical therapies not recommended
claims.source_text: Complementary therapies and herbal preparations (e.g. black cohosh, phytoestrogens) have insufficient evidence of benefit, can cause adverse effects, and are not recommended … Custom-compounded, bioidentical hormone therapy is also not recommended because of limited dose regulation and lack of safety data

claims.claim: NAMS no longer recommends clonidine or pregabalin
claims.source_text: The North American Menopause Society no longer recommends clonidine or pregabalin for treatment of vasomotor symptoms because of their adverse effects; however, they are still used in some instances in Australia

claims.claim: Lifestyle and CBT
claims.source_text: Lifestyle modifications such as exercise, weight loss and reducing alcohol consumption may be helpful for some women. These measures may not reduce the severity of symptoms but may make them more manageable … Cognitive behavioural therapy can reduce the impact of vasomotor symptoms and alleviate sleep disturbance

claims.claim: Emerging treatments estetrol and fezolinetant
claims.source_text: Estetrol may provide some safety advantages through reduced effects on liver and breast tissue … A 2023 randomised placebo-controlled trial reported the neurokinin 3 receptor antagonist, fezolinetant, was effective and well tolerated for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms

claims.claim: Estrogen suitable for osteoporosis under 60
claims.source_text: Estrogen therapy is suitable for the management of osteoporosis or low bone density in women younger than 60 years of age

claims.claim: Mintzes challenges the effectiveness characterisation and symptom list
claims.source_text: contains unsupported claims. Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is characterised as 'highly effective' and 'the most effective treatment' for menopausal symptoms. A list of symptoms includes sleep disturbance, mood changes, cognitive concerns and musculoskeletal symptoms, which are not actually menopausal

claims.claim: Benefits and harms are largely unquantified
claims.source_text: Neither the purported benefits nor harms of MHT are quantified, except for a doubling or tripling of venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk. However, absolute risk of VTE is described only as remaining low. Risks of heart attack, stroke and breast cancer, similarly, remain unquantified

claims.claim: The cardiovascular claim rests on a guideline with industry-funded authors
claims.source_text: The claim that menopause - rather than ageing per se - is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease is supported not by research evidence, but by an International Menopause Society guideline. … Among the guideline's 21 authors, 14 report pharmaceutical industry funding

claims.claim: The Cochrane review conclusion quoted against the article
claims.source_text: this review concludes there is 'strong evidence that treatment with hormone therapy in post-menopausal women overall, for either primary or secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease events has little if any benefit

claims.claim: Million Women absolute breast cancer numbers by duration
claims.source_text: based on the UK Million Women study, 5 years use of estrogen plus progestogen leads to 6 extra breast cancers per 1000 users; 10 years use leads to 19 extra breast cancers per 1000 users

claims.claim: Fugh-Berman states only hot flushes and vaginal dryness are proven menopausal
claims.source_text: the only symptoms proven to be associated with menopause are hot flushes and vaginal dryness

claims.claim: Mintzes declares no conflicts
claims.source_text: Conflicts of interest: none declared

claims.claim: Fugh-Berman declares expert witness work on MHT promotion
claims.source_text: Adriane Fugh-Berman is a paid … expert witness in litigation regarding pharmaceutical marketing, and has … previously been a paid expert witness in litigation regarding the promotion of … menopausal hormone therapy

claims.claim: Authors give the absolute VTE rates
claims.source_text: The baseline risk for VTE is 1 to 2 events in 1000 person-years; … for women taking MHT, the risk is 2 to 3 events in … 1000 person-years, which is considered low

claims.claim: Authors argue breast cancer risk should not be attributed to all MHT equally
claims.source_text: Until breast cancer rates have been studied for women using more modern … forms of MHT, we would argue against attributing an increased risk of breast … cancer to all forms of MHT equally

claims.claim: Authors clarify they relied on the Cochrane subgroup analysis
claims.source_text: We were referring to the subgroup analysis in the Cochrane review that focused … on women starting MHT within 10 years after menopause and showed lower … mortality and coronary heart disease in this group. … We have stated that MHT is not indicated for primary prevention of … cardiovascular disease

claims.claim: Authors argue route and progestogen type were omitted from the critique
claims.source_text: fails to discuss that this is associated with the route … of administration of estrogen and the type of progestogen used

claims.claim: Magraith and Jang hold Australasian Menopause Society offices
claims.source_text: Immediate-past president, Australasian Menopause Society … President-elect, Australasian Menopause Society
